title: The random-walk pattern probability characterization conjecture
statement:
Let $S_n$ be the symmetric group, let $X_1,X_2,\ldots,X_{n-1}$ be independent identically distributed random variables, and let $p(X_1,X_2,\ldots,X_{n-1})$ denote the permutation pattern associated with their outcomes. Let $\sim$ be the equivalence relation on permutations defined by valid flips. **Random-walk pattern probability characterization conjecture.** For $\pi,\tau\in S_n$, one has

$$
\mathbb{P}(p(X_1,X_2,\ldots,X_{n-1})=\pi)=\mathbb{P}(p(X_1,X_2,\ldots,X_{n-1})=\tau)
$$

for every probability distribution on the i.i.d. random variables $X_1,X_2,\ldots,X_{n-1}$ if and only if $\pi\sim\tau$. The preceding results characterize the equivalence classes using valid flips; the conjecture asserts that these classes are exactly the classes of permutations having equal occurrence probabilities for every step distribution, and the authors state that they are working on a proof.
source_name: Sergi Elizalde and Megan Martinez, “The frequency of pattern occurrence in random walks”, arXiv:1412.0692 (2014).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1412.0692

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2014).
